skill.name: agent-tools
skill.description: Use the inference.sh CLI to discover and run hosted AI apps for images, videos, LLMs, search, 3D generation, and utility workflows.
skill.summary: Run hosted inference.sh AI apps from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code with guided CLI commands.
skill.author: inference-sh-3

security_audit.summary: Confirmed risks include remote installer guidance that pipes network content into a shell. The manual install also uses dynamic shell substitution to select a binary URL. Most other static hits are Markdown formatting, placeholder API key documentation, or ordinary product links.

remediation.issue: Remote installer commands pipe downloaded content directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipe-to-shell flow with pinned release downloads, documented checksums, signature verification, and explicit user confirmation before installation.

remediation.issue: Manual install guidance builds a download URL with shell command substitution from a remote manifest.
remediation.suggestion: Provide a structured installer or package-manager command that validates a pinned artifact before extraction and installation.

remediation.issue: The skill can trigger external account actions such as posting to X.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation for any social posting, following, liking, retweeting, or direct-message action.

remediation.issue: API key examples may lead users to paste real credentials into prompts.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should use local environment variables or secret managers and avoid sharing live keys in chat.

content.user_title: Run AI Apps with inference.sh CLI
content.value_statement: Agents often need one way to discover and run hosted AI tools. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh CLI workflows for models, media, search, and task tracking.
actual_capabilities: Runs inference.sh apps through the infsh CLI when the CLI is installed and authenticated.
Shows commands for discovering apps by category, search term, featured status, or new status.
Generates sample app inputs and saves them to local files through infsh commands.
Submits image, video, LLM, search, 3D, and utility tasks supported by inference.sh.
Tracks long-running tasks and saves returned results through infsh task commands.
Provides authentication, API key, shell completion, and CLI command references.
limitations: Requires an installed infsh CLI and an inference.sh account.
Does not validate remote installer code or hosted app behavior.
Can only run apps that inference.sh exposes and the account can access.
Actions with external services, such as X posting, may have irreversible effects.

use_cases.title: Prototype media assets
use_cases.description: Generate images, videos, speech, or 3D outputs from hosted models without managing local GPU infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Compare hosted models
use_cases.description: Search available apps, inspect model details, and run approved prompts across supported LLM and media providers.

use_cases.title: Automate model tasks
use_cases.description: Submit long-running jobs, track task status, and save results for repeatable team workflows.

prompt_templates.title: List image apps
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to list inference.sh apps for image generation and summarize the best candidates for product mockups.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare sample input
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to get sample input for falai/flux-dev-lora, save it, and explain each required field before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Run and track video
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to run google/veo-3-1-fast with my approved prompt, then track the task until a result is available.

prompt_templates.title: Build a model workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to design a workflow that searches with Tavily, summarizes with Claude, and creates an image. Ask before any external action.

output_examples.input: Find image models for product mockups.
output: The skill lists relevant image apps and highlights model strengths.
It recommends checking app details before spending credits.
It suggests generating a sample input before the first run.

output_examples.input: Run a long video generation task and keep status.
output_examples.output: The skill submits the approved task, reports the task identifier, checks status, and points to the saved result when available.

output_examples.input: Prepare a safe X posting workflow.
output_examples.output: The skill drafts the post, requests explicit approval, and runs the authorized CLI action only after approval.

best_practices: Confirm the target app, input file, and spending impact before running long jobs.
Use sample input commands before submitting a new model task.
Keep API keys in environment variables or secret stores outside chat transcripts.
anti_patterns: Piping remote installers directly to a shell during unattended agent sessions.
Running X posting, follow, like, retweet, or message actions without explicit approval.
Using broad app names without checking the exact namespace and version.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps agents use the infsh CLI to discover, run, and track hosted inference.sh apps.

faq.question: Does it install inference.sh automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents installation commands, but users should approve and verify any install step.

faq.question: What accounts or tools are required?
faq.answer: You need the infsh CLI, an inference.sh account, and credentials with access to the selected apps.

faq.question: Can it run Claude or OpenRouter models?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples for OpenRouter and Claude models exposed through inference.sh apps.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets?
faq.answer: No. It documents the INFSH_API_KEY environment variable and expects users to manage credentials securely.

faq.question: Is social media automation safe?
faq.answer: It can affect external accounts. Always require explicit approval before posting, following, liking, retweeting, or messaging.
